sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation

items.q: Fill up (opening line of the chapter): Primary Biliary Cirrhosis / Primary Biliary Cholangitis is the cardinal example of ______ cholestasis.
items.exp: The chapter opens: 'Cardinal example of intrahepatic cholestasis.' (Book p1020)

items.q: Judge the two statements from the printed definition of PBC: I It is an autoimmune disease with chronic progressive non-suppurative inflammatory destruction. II The target is the large extrahepatic bile ducts.
items.exp: Definition: autoimmune, chronic progressive non-suppurative inflammatory destruction of SMALL intrahepatic / intralobular bile ducts — not the large extrahepatic ducts. (Book p1020)

items.q: According to the printed definition, the destruction of small intrahepatic / intralobular bile ducts in PBC is mediated by which immune arm?
opts: Both T-cell and B-cell, with T-cell predominating over B-cell
T-cell only, with no antibody contribution
items.exp: The arrow below the definition reads 'mediated by both T-cell > B-cell'. (Book p1020)

items.q: Antimitochondrial antibody (AMA) is printed as positive in what proportion of PBC patients?
items.exp: 'Antimitochondrial Ab (AMA) 95%.' (ANA is the 50% antibody listed later on p1021.) (Book p1020)

items.q: Fill up: In PBC the antimitochondrial antibody is directed against ______.
items.exp: 'Against : PDHE2.' The footnote to the Note table expands it: 'PDHE2 : Pyruvate dehydrogenase enzyme type-2'. (Book p1020)

items.q: Match each column of the Note table (Hepatic vs Cholestatic pattern) with its printed content — 1) Hepatic 2) Cholestatic … A) Fatigue and pruritus, progressing through complete destruction of bile duct to jaundice (poor prognosis) B) Jaundice as the predominant feature
items.exp: Note table: Hepatic column = 'Jaundice (predominant feature)'; Cholestatic column = 'Fatigue & pruritus → complete destruction of bile duct → Jaundice (Poor prognosis)'. (Book p1020)

items.q: A patient with PBC who for years had only fatigue and pruritus now develops jaundice. Per the Note table's cholestatic column, what does this jaundice signify?
opts: Complete destruction of the bile ducts and a poor prognosis
Onset of the hepatic pattern, which carries the better prognosis
Transient viral superinfection unrelated to duct loss
Successful response to UDCA with ductular regeneration
items.exp: In the cholestatic column the arrow runs fatigue & pruritus → 'Complete destruction of bile duct' → 'Jaundice (Poor prognosis)'. (Book p1020)

items.q: What female-to-male ratio and age band are printed under 'Prevalence' of PBC?
Which of the following is NOT one of the three disease associations listed for PBC on this page?
items.exp: Disease association list: Sjogren syndrome with arthritis, Distal RTA (Type 1), Gallstones. Ulcerative colitis is the PSC association (p1021). (Book p1020)

items.q: Diagnostic algorithm: a patient with cholestasis undergoes ultrasound. Duct dilatation is ABSENT. What is the next printed step?
opts: Check AMA antibody; if positive, diagnose PBC
Proceed directly to liver transplant listing
Start empirical UDCA and reassess in 6 months
items.exp: Algorithm: Patient with cholestasis → Ultrasound: look for duct dilatation → −ve → AMA Ab → +ve → PBC. (Book p1020)

items.q: In the same algorithm, ultrasound shows duct dilatation (+ve). What does the book direct?
opts: Perform liver biopsy for florid duct lesion
items.exp: Ultrasound +ve for duct dilatation → 'Refer to surgery' (obstructive / extrahepatic cause). (Book p1020)

items.q: Presentation of PBC — judge: I Asymptomatic is the most common presentation. II Pruritus is the most common symptom.
items.exp: 'Asymptomatic (m/c presentation)', 'Fatigue (m/c symptom)', then Pruritus as a separate bullet. (Book p1020)

items.q: Jaundice occurs in what percentage of PBC patients, and how is it characterised in the presentation list?
Fill up the bracket exactly as printed beside hypercholesterolemia in the PBC presentation list: 'Hypercholesterolemia (Against : ______)'.
items.exp: The bullet reads 'Hypercholesterolemia (Against : Dihydrolipoyl transacetylase)' — the printed bracket names the E2 (dihydrolipoyl transacetylase) component that AMA targets; it is the antibody target, not a mechanism of hypercholesterolaemia. (Book p1020)

items.q: Match the printed frequencies in the PBC presentation list — 1) Hepatomegaly 2) Splenomegaly 3) Jaundice … A) <15% B) 10% C) 30–40%
Which of the following is NOT listed among the PBC presentation bullets on this page?
items.exp: The list: asymptomatic, fatigue, pruritus, jaundice, hypercholesterolemia, xanthelasmas, hyperpigmentation, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, steatorrhea. K-F rings belong to Wilson's disease. (Book p1020)

items.q: Steatorrhea in PBC is attributed on this page to which mechanism?

The flowchart under steatorrhea lists three consequences of fat malabsorption and one downstream effect. Match — 1) Diarrhea 2) ↓ Fat soluble vitamin 3) ↓ Vitamin D absorption … A) leads to metabolic bone disease B) direct consequence of fat malabsorption (first arrow) C) direct consequence of fat malabsorption (second arrow)
items.exp: Fat malabsorption → Diarrhea; → ↓ Fat soluble vitamin; → ↓ Vitamin D absorption → metabolic bone disease. (Book p1020)
